interpretations: Treat each funding source, including missing funding as a source, as a group of spatial records; size is the number of records. Select sources whose counts exceed the mean source count, then return one row with the mean of their per-source average `boxy / boxz` ratios, the sum of their counts, and the mean amount by which their counts exceed the mean
Use the same calculation, but count only spatial records with both `boxy` and `boxz` present when measuring each source’s size
Use the same calculation, but define size as the number of distinct projects with spatial records for each funding source
Use the same calculation, but define each source’s ratio as `AVG(boxy) / AVG(boxz)` rather than `AVG(boxy / boxz)`
Use spatial-record count as size, but calculate the final ratio across all qualifying spatial records, weighting sources with more records more heavily
Use distinct-project count as size, but calculate the final ratio across all qualifying spatial records, weighting sources according to their numbers of records
Use spatial-record count as size, but calculate the final average excess weighted by each qualifying source’s record count
Use spatial-record count as size, but calculate the comparison average only across sources with a nonmissing funding value while still allowing the missing-source group to qualify
Use spatial-record count as size, but exclude the missing-source group from both the comparison average and the final result
Treat size as the sum of `aream2` for each funding source; select sources above the mean source total and summarize their ratios, combined area, and mean excess area
Treat size as the average `aream2` per spatial record for each funding source; select sources above the mean of those averages and summarize their ratios, combined source sizes, and mean excess size
Treat size as the sum of `volm3` for each funding source; select sources above the mean source total and summarize their ratios, combined volume, and mean excess volume
Treat size as the average `volm3` per spatial record for each funding source; select sources above the mean of those averages and summarize their ratios, combined source sizes, and mean excess size

Treat size as the sum of bounding-box volumes `boxx * boxy * boxz` for each funding source; select sources above the mean source total and summarize their ratios, combined volume, and mean excess volume
Treat size as the sum of bounding-box Y–Z areas `boxy * boxz` for each funding source; select sources above the mean source total and summarize their ratios, combined area, and mean excess area
Treat size as the average bounding-box volume (`boxx * boxy * boxz`) per spatial record for each funding source

queries:
WITH source_counts AS (
  SELECT p.fundflux, COUNT(*) AS record_count,
         AVG(s.boxy / s.boxz) AS avg_ratio
  FROM scanspatial AS s
  JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
source_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(record_count) AS mean_count
  FROM source_counts
)
SELECT AVG(sc.avg_ratio),
       SUM(sc.record_count),
       AVG(sc.record_count - sm.mean_count)
FROM source_counts AS sc
CROSS JOIN source_mean AS sm
WHERE sc.record_count > sm.mean_count

SELECT p.fundflux,
       COUNT(DISTINCT ss.arcref) AS size
FROM projects AS p
JOIN scanspatial AS ss
  ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
GROUP BY p.fundflux

SELECT p.fundflux,
       AVG(s.boxy) / NULLIF(AVG(s.boxz), 0) AS ratio
FROM projects AS p
JOIN scanspatial AS s ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry
GROUP BY p.fundflux
